title: MRO CRISM map-projected targeted summary parameters (MTRDR)
reference: Viviano-Beck et al. (2014), Revised CRISM spectral parameters and summary products, J. Geophys. Res. Planets 119, 1403-1431

scenes.note: Full-resolution targeted observation at 18 m/px. Covers the AOI across its full width but stops short at both ends in latitude, so it supplies most of the AOI and none of the extreme north or south.

Half-resolution long targeted observation at 36 m/px. Its footprint contains the whole AOI, so it fills what the FRT scene misses. Used only where the FRT scene has no valid value, and flagged per cell in coverage.png because it is half the resolution.

resample: Nearest neighbour from 18 m/px (primary) and 36 m/px (gap-fill) onto 14.29 m cells. This is an upsample, so the geochemistry is blockier than the terrain under it. Nearest rather than bilinear because interpolating would place index values between cells the instrument never measured.

coverage_mask.encoding: 8-bit PNG; 0 = no CRISM coverage, 1 = primary scene, 2 = gap-fill scene

bands.name: BD530_2
bands.mineralogy: nanophase and crystalline iron oxide, hematite
bands.encoding: 8-bit PNG. 0 = no CRISM value. 1..255 linear over scale_min..scale_max, so index = scale_min + (v - 1) / 254 * (scale_max - scale_min).
bands.scale_note: scale_min is the 1st percentile, not the minimum: the lowest one per cent of cells render at level 1. scale_max is the true maximum, so no detection is clipped.

bands_note: Band order is read from the ENVI header at run time, never hard-coded: the header's `band names` list is the only authority for which of the 60 planes is which parameter, and both scenes were checked to carry the same order.
no_data: The sentinel is the ENVI header's `data ignore value` (65535.0). The PDS label carries no NULL keyword, so the header has to be read.
caveat: These are spectral indices, not mineral abundances. A high index means the shape the parameter measures is present in that pixel's spectrum; it is evidence for a mineral group, not a measurement of how much is there. Thin dust cover, slope and illumination all move these numbers.
